projects.title: Maxwell's point charges
projects.dek: How many points of balance can a few electric charges have? Exact, computer-checked counts for four, five and six charges.
projects.status: Claimed · computer-checked counts · not reviewed by a person
projects.one_line: Foundation0's first physics study, a project of its physics0 hub: Maxwell said n positive point charges have at most (n−1)² points of balance. Interval-arithmetic certificates, each confirmed by a second program that shares no code, give exact counts: 9 for four charges (the bound), 24 for an explicit five-charge counterexample, and 29 for six. Done by Claude (Anthropic); not yet reviewed by a person.

stats.label: equilibria for four charges: exactly Maxwell's bound (n−1)², which a 2026 paper knew no configuration to reach for n > 3
equilibria, exactly, in an explicit five-charge counterexample to Maxwell (bound 16); every one enclosed, none degenerate
equilibria for six charges, above Maxwell's bound for six
verifiers that share no code confirm every count; both reject four deliberately corrupted certificates

projects.title: mobius-x1
projects.dek: A claimed way to compute a basic transform on bits (the GF(2) Möbius transform) with fewer one-bit XOR steps than Yates’ 1937 recipe, for astronomically large inputs.
projects.one_line: A claimed, AI-assisted proof that the subset-parity (Möbius/zeta) transform over GF(2) needs asymptotically fewer XOR gates than Yates' 1937 ½·N·log₂N recipe, built by transplanting an AI-generated OpenAI Fourier-transform construction into bit arithmetic; the saving appears only when k has billions of digits. Aska's team of AI agents contributed the full-network check of the strongest version (Theorem 2).
